messages.msg-match-a-near-zero: The graph is not a parabola while a is at 0. Move a off 0, then submit again.
messages.msg-match-all: The graph matches f(x) = (x + 3)² + 1. The vertex marker is at (−3, 1), and the parabola opens upward.
messages.msg-match-wrong-opening: The vertex is at (−3, 1), matching the target. Your graph opens downward; the target opens upward. Keep the vertex where it is and change the sign of a.
messages.msg-match-wrong-abs-a: The vertex is at (−3, 1) and the graph opens upward, like the target. The stretch does not yet match — your a is {a}, and you want a = 1. Keep the vertex and change the stretch.
messages.msg-match-h-not-k: Your vertex is in the right horizontal position. The vertex is at ({h}, {k}); the target vertex is at (−3, 1). The x-coordinates match; the y-coordinates do not. Adjust the control that shifts the parabola up or down.
messages.msg-match-other: The vertex is at ({h}, {k}), but the target vertex is at (−3, 1) with the parabola opening upward. Compare those two points and the opening, then adjust.
messages.msg-match-explain: You matched the target. How did you read the vertex from f(x) = (x + 3)² + 1? What changed when you moved from f(x) = 2(x + 3)² + 1 to that equation?
messages.msg-match-follow-up: Where is the vertex marker now, and where do you want it? Name both points.
messages.hint-match-1-live-equation: Look at the live equation labelled Vertex form, above the graph. You want it to read f(x) = (x + 3)² + 1.
messages.hint-match-2-brackets-to-h: Vertex form uses (x − h). Rewrite the brackets to match that pattern, then read h.
messages.hint-match-3-vertex-marker: The labelled point on the graph is the vertex (h, k). Compare it with the equation you want.
messages.msg-predict-h-uncertain: More than the horizontal position changed, or it is unclear which control you moved. Which quantity did you mean to change: a, h, or k? Reset if you need a clean start, then move only h.
messages.msg-predict-h-not-moved: The vertex is still at x = −3. You have not yet moved h.
messages.msg-predict-h-match: The vertex is now at x = {observed_h}, which matches the x you predicted ({predicted_vertex_x}).
messages.msg-predict-h-differ: The vertex is at x = {observed_h}. You predicted x = {predicted_vertex_x}. Look at the labelled vertex and the live equation labelled Vertex form, then adjust h or revise the prediction.
messages.msg-predict-h-interpret: You moved the vertex horizontally. What changed on the graph and in the equation? What stayed the same? Does the expanded equation in standard form show a different parabola, or the same one?
messages.msg-predict-h-follow-up: How did you connect the equation to that x-value? Match the brackets to (x − h) and compare with the labelled vertex.
messages.hint-predict-h-1-name-x-first: Write the vertex x you expect before you move h.
messages.hint-predict-h-2-watch-marker: Move only h. Watch the labelled vertex and the dashed vertical line.
messages.hint-predict-h-3-equation-after-move: After the move, read h from (x − h) in the live equation labelled Vertex form and compare it with the labelled vertex.
messages.msg-expand-match: Your expansion matches. 2(x + 3)² + 1 and 2x² + 12x + 19 are the same parabola — not a new graph. Check that a few table points sit on both forms.
messages.msg-expand-differ: You entered a = {standard_a}, b = {standard_b}, c = {standard_c}. Those coefficients are not the expansion of f(x) = 2(x + 3)² + 1. Square the binomial first, multiply by a = 2, then add k = 1.
messages.hint-expand-1-square-the-binomial: Expand (x + 3)² first for this starting equation.
messages.hint-expand-3-add-k: Then add k = 1. Compare graphs only after the expansion is written.
messages.msg-fresh-reading-match: Your vertex, axis, and maximum-or-minimum reading match this equation. You may now move exactly one of a, h, or k to see what changes.
messages.msg-fresh-vertex-differs: You named the point ({named_vertex_x}, {named_vertex_y}). Match the brackets to (x − h) and read k as the y-coordinate of the vertex, then name the point again.
messages.msg-fresh-axis-differs: The vertex you named matches this equation. The axis you wrote was {named_axis}. The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex.
messages.msg-fresh-extreme-differs: The vertex and axis you named match this equation. Look at the sign of a to decide whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum, then name that again.
messages.msg-fresh-explain: How did you read the vertex, the axis, and whether this is a maximum or a minimum from this equation? If you expanded it, would the fountain-shaped curve move?
messages.hint-fresh-1-match-brackets: Match (x − 2) to (x − h) before you move anything.
messages.hint-fresh-2-axis-vertical: The axis is the vertical line through the vertex.
messages.hint-fresh-3-sign-of-a: Maximum or minimum comes from the sign of a, not from k or from which quadrant the vertex sits in.
